title: 16p11.2 microdeletion enhances gene expression variability between human iPSC-derived forebrain interneuron progenitor cells in culture
abstract: The 574-kb 16p11.2 microdeletion raises risk for neurodevelopmental and energy-balance conditions, particularly autism and obesity, with considerable clinical heterogeneity. Using human iPSC-derived ventral telencephalic interneuron progenitors isogenic except for a heterozygous 16p11.2 microdeletion, single-cell RNA-seq revealed hundreds of differentially expressed transcripts (cell signaling, chromatin, neurodevelopment) and significantly greater transcript-level variability between heterozygous progenitors than isogenic wild-type, for regulon gene sets and random gene sets, indicating the locus itself has a genome-wide transcription-stabilizing property. The most variable regulons were enriched for cell-cycle genes and often regulated by transcription factors linked to autism and/or obesity.
